For those of you who have been living under a rock, and missed the hype back in 2011, the Kel-Tec KSG is a dual magazine tube fed bullpup style pump 12 gauge boasting a 12+1 round capacity, coming in just over 2' (26").

Having owned mine for a little over 2.5 years, I've had ample opportunity to play with it, shoot the snot out of it, and really get a feel for the shotgun, this brings me to my first downside to the little thumper. It is short, with a DANGEROUSLY short stroke on the pump, that takes a lot of time to get used to (if you are used to handling 870's or Mossy 500's). Guys are loosing their hands to this blood hungry rabid bully because of either failures of their forward grip, or in my opinion, because they treat it like a long stroke 870, and slide that hand forward while shooting (it's easy to see how it's done when you fire one). But aside from the risks associated with running this thing fast and loose, it really is a pretty fun shotgun, that has many advantages.

Another downside to the KSG is the recoil, for more sensitive shooters, this thing will rock a shoulder a little more than comfortable. Being short, light, and fun to shoot, allows for a bruise to develop pretty quick. One friend of mine who is no stranger to traditional shotguns changed his mind on purchasing a KSG after getting kicked by this little mule, and opted to stick with his Ithaca M37 (and I don't blame him) for his "home defense" choice.

Now that the negatives are all out of the way, give me an opportunity to tell you what I DO like about the KSG:

It's short, I mean really, really short, 26" may not sound too short until you handle this thing, and feel how maneuverable it can be, some may count this as a downside, but for me, I like it! Not just short, but also light, and well balanced when fully loaded, shooting clay pigeons with this thing is fast and fun, and nothing feels quite like it.

Magazine capacity is nice, and once you get used to the toggle that changes from what tube the rounds are feeding from, it allows for a new dynamic in your shotgun shooting. Fill one tube with bird shot, and the other with slugs, and switch between the two on the fly, like having the versatility of a double trigger SXS only with a helluva lot more rounds.

Some guys may like the Taci-cool-lol look and rail system on this thing, I admit, I do have a Laser Genetics ND3 AR hanging on the side of mine, and I love the results, but on a whole, I'm more of a "wood meets metal"-"keep your black gun" type of guy.

Reliability is solid on the KSG, and this is important to me, with around 2000 rounds through mine, I've yet to have a malfunction that was not attributed to user error or ammo, and it happily eats anything I've fed it. So the reliability of a proven pump platform is there, just in a more complicated (dual tube feeding) way.

After a few years, and more than a few boxes of shells, I can say that I like my KSG, but don't Love it. It is a gimmicky (just opinion here) shotgun that is fun to shoot, show off at the range, and handle, but for Real Life applications, other more cost effective guns do the same job. Like any new firearm, it has a learning curve that may require you to re-train your habits of how you operate the thing (keep your damned hand on the pump) and familiarize yourself with it well before you show off like an idiot (or just don't be an idiot). I won't be selling mine, it's a keeper, but it took a lot of time and debate for me to come to that conclusion.
